<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os lint (command, 50 pages)`, `/meta/:type/:name (route, 50 pages)`
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bcdad83443ce6621d98bf2e8d0905c8ea8dd1c1a` — the merge of head `f0520d6a23b793862eaa00fdb16889deff6bfe27` into base `c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bcdad83443ce6621d98bf2e8d0905c8ea8dd1c1a && git checkout bcdad83443ce6621d98bf2e8d0905c8ea8dd1c1a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe f0520d6a23b793862eaa00fdb16889deff6bfe27 && git checkout -B drift-repro c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe && git merge --no-ff f0520d6a23b793862eaa00fdb16889deff6bfe27

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- **Read in the dev's risk order**
  1. **`draftPublishVerdictOf`** reads `item._diagnostics` only when the read's `version` equals the saved receipt's `version`. Another row's answer (the published item served to a caller the door does not admit to drafts, or a later draft) yields `verdict: null` with an `unread` reason, and nothing is printed as the draft's verdict. It is pinned for an equal version, a different one, `null`, and a missing `_diagnostics`.
     - **Nit:** the guard is skipped when the receipt carries no string `version`, so the read's `_diagnostics` is then taken unguarded. The current door always returns the token (#22114), so this is not reachable today. Failing closed (treating a non-string `savedVersion` as unread) is a one-line hardening for an older server, and nothing is owed.
  2. **`metaRegisterOptions`** throws `DRAFT_NEEDS_PACKAGE_REFUSAL` inside the options builder. `run()` calls it first, before `createApiClient`, `requireAuth` or the file read. Pinned: exit 1, no client made, nothing on the wire. `--mode publish` and an unflagged run build no `mode`, so the request is byte-identical to before.      - A rule that read anything beside the collection (including `ownKeys`, and the filter judge, which marks `objects`) is listed under `notJudged` with the keys it read, and its findings are dropped.

     That is the conservative side: a cross-item rule cannot report a false finding on an item judged alone. The two limits are stated in the docs: same-type references see no sibling, and a whole-stack walker is listed even where it would have judged alone. `familiesNotRun` names the three `os lint` families.
- **The deliberate choice** — `--mode draft` with a `valid: false` verdict exits 0. Accepted: the save succeeded and the draft is stored, and staging an unpublishable draft is what drafts are for. The verdict prints as warning and error lines, and it is also `publishVerdict` on `--format json|yaml`. `os lint --item` is the failing pre-flight, with an exit code read as a project run's, `--strict` included. The flag help, the changeset and `cli.mdx` each say it.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set: no `packages/spec` file, no REST route, no metadata-protocol or server-side code is in the diff, so what the runtime accepts and what a metadata author can write is unchanged. The diff changes three public surfaces, all widenings, and one internal refactor.

- **D1 · `@objectstack/client` `meta.getItem` `state?: 'active' | 'draft'`, on both declarations: RIGHT.** `ObjectStackClient.meta.getItem` and `ScopedEnvironmentClient.meta.getItem` (`packages/client/src/index.ts`) each add one line, `if (options?.state === 'draft') params.set('state', 'draft')`, after the existing `package` and `callerPackage` params. An absent option, or `'active'`, adds no parameter, so the bytes sent are the same as before. `meta-get-item-draft-read.test.ts` pins this with a control on both surfaces (no options, `packageId` only, and `packageId` plus `'active'`, each giving the old URL). The spelling matches the client's existing `deleteItem` `state` (`index.ts:1156`), so the SDK has one way to say it. The response type does not move: `GetMetaItemResponseSchema.version` already says that `?state=draft` reads the draft row's token (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`). The premise that the client had no draft read holds: `getDraft` exists only on the ui-side `MetadataClient`, not in `@objectstack/client`.
- **D2 · `os meta register --mode draft|publish`: RIGHT.** It is a `Flags.string` with `options: ['draft', 'publish']` and no default. `metaRegisterOptions` maps only `draft` to `mode: 'draft'`. An unflagged run and a `--mode publish` run build the same options object as before, which is `undefined` when no other flag is set, so they send the same single `PUT`. The read-back (`reportDraft`) is reached only when `options?.mode === 'draft'`, so no `GET` follows any other run. The integration file's negative control pins this on the real `RestServer`, protocol and SQLite.
- **D3 · The D4 refusal: RIGHT.** `DRAFT_NEEDS_PACKAGE_REFUSAL` is thrown inside `metaRegisterOptions`, and `run()` calls that first, before `createApiClient`. So no client exists and nothing reaches the wire, and no path saves before the refusal. An empty `--package` still gets the existing `EMPTY_PACKAGE_SAVE_REFUSAL` first, which is consistent. The JSON face reports the refusal through the existing catch (`success: false`, exit 1).
- **D4 · The verdict read and its version guard: RIGHT.**
  - `draftPublishVerdictOf` accepts the read only when its `version` equals the save receipt's `version`.
  - `SaveMetaItemResponseSchema.version` is required, so on every 2xx the guard is always armed, never skipped.
  - The server folds the verdict into `_diagnostics` on the strict draft read (`serveDraft` and `draftPublishJudgement` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`, #26707). The CLI computes no verdict of its own.
  - When the version differs, the read fails, or the read has no `_diagnostics`, the run prints `Publish verdict not printed: REASON`. The JSON face carries `publishVerdict: null` plus `publishVerdictUnread`. It never shows another row's diagnostics.
- **D5 · The printed Studio route: RIGHT.** `/studio/PKG/interfaces?changes=review` is the off-pillar form of `studioChangesReviewTarget` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/studioChangesLink.ts`).
- **D6 · `os lint --item FILE --type TYPE`: RIGHT.**
  - The flags are new and refused in every combination they cannot serve: `--type` alone, `--item` alone, either with a config path, `--eval` or `--score`. Each exits 1 on both faces.
  - `resolveItemType` accepts only `SINGULAR_TO_PLURAL` keys or their plurals.
  - `judgeItemAlone` classifies each `authoringRulesFor('lint')` entry by the top-level keys it reads through the proxy. An `ownKeys` trap counts as reading every key. A call to `judgeFilter` counts as reading `objects`. Both choices err toward "not judged", which is the property fork 2 = A keeps.
  - The header states the measurement's two blind spots. One is the same-type reference case. I read one such rule, `lintSummaryRollups`: an absent child object makes it silent (`data-model-rules.ts`, "The child object — not judged"), so that blind spot loses a finding rather than inventing one.

Findings:

- **F1 · nit:** the `client-sdk.mdx` snippet `draft.item._diagnostics?.valid` does not type-check as written, because `GetMetaItemResponse.item` is `z.unknown()`. The CLI itself casts (`read?.item as { _diagnostics?: ... }`). The snippet should show the cast, or read through a typed local. This is docs only and does not affect the contract.
- **F2 · nit:** the PR body quotes the D4 refusal as ending `--package PACKAGE_ID`, but `DRAFT_NEEDS_PACKAGE_REFUSAL` spells it as `--package` followed by an angle-bracketed `id`. The body sanitizer probably forced the paraphrase. The code is the authority. Nothing to change in the tree.
- **F3 · nit:** the `os lint --item` text face ends with "Run `os lint` on the project, or publish the draft, for those." Since this PR, the publish verdict is available without going live: `os meta register --mode draft` reads it back. Pointing to that is the safer way to say it.
